description: Demolition of existing rear outrigger extensions; erection of a ground floor single storey rear extension; internal refurbishment; landscaping works to the front and rear; and, installation of new front boundary treatment.
decision_conditions:
The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission.


REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).

The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.


REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.

<p>Prior to superstructure works, detailed specification, a drainage layout and a management &amp; maintenance plan (where applicable) of at least one suitable sustainable drainage system (i.e. water butt with overflow, raingarden, bioretention planter box, living roof (substrate depth of 80-150mm excluding the vegetative mat), permeable paving etc.) shall be submitted to, and approved by the LPA, in consultation with the LLFA. If soakaways i.e. plastic modules and soakaway rings are used, an infiltration test must be carried out to ensure that the capacity of the soil is suitable for infiltration. It must be demonstrated that there will be no increase in surface water flow being discharged offsite and an overall reduction in peak flow rate and volume. The development shall be implemented as per the apprpved details.&nbsp;</p><div>REASON: To promote sustainable water management and prevent increased surface water runoff into the local network.</div>

<p>All new underground utility apparatus, including drainage, shall be routed and installed outside the Root Protection Area(s) (RPAs) shown on the approved drawings. Should it not be feasible to route new underground utility apparatus outside the RPAs of retained trees, trenchless insertion methods (as detailed in BS 5837:2012, Table 3) shall be employed for their installation within the RPAs, with entry and retrieval pits sited outside the RPAs. No other new underground utilities shall be installed within the RPAs of retained trees without prior written consent from the local planning authority (LPA). Any such works, if permitted, shall be carried out in strict accordance with the principles of BS 5837:2012 "Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction – Recommendations" and the National Joint Utilities Group Guidelines for the planning, installation and maintenance of utility apparatus in proximity to trees, Volume 4, Issue 2 (2007) (or any standard that reproduces or replaces this standard).</p><p>REASON: To safeguard existing tree(s) in the interests of visual amenities and long-term tree health. Prior approval is required to ensure that important trees are not permanently damaged or lost due to root disturbance or changes in soil hydrology.</p><div><br></div>

<p>Prior to the commencement of the relevant part of the work, the applicant shall submit, and have approved in writing by the local planning authority, a detailed layout, cross sections (scale 1:20), full specifications and a detailed management and maintenance plan of the biodiverse roof with a minimum substrate depth of 80mm, not including the vegetative mat. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details thus approved and shall be fully implemented before the premises are first occupied. </p><p>REASON: In the interest of enhancing biodiversity and managing flood risk and providing a sustainable drainage system.</p>

<p>A. Prior to the commencement of development, a qualified tree specialist must be appointed to provide arboricultural supervision and inspection. The details of this appointment and the specialist's responsibilities must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The submission should include the methodology and programme for reporting, as well as a timetable for inspections that includes the following critical stages:</p><p>- Satisfactory installation of tree protection measures.</p><p>- Demolition, excavation, and construction within the Root Protection Areas (RPAs) of trees T4, T5, and T6.</p><p>- Removal of tree protection measures at the end of the development.</p><p>The approved works must be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details. </p><p>B. Upon completion of the development, a report from the appointed arboriculturist must be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. This report must confirm that all tree protection measures and tree works were carried out in accordance with the approved plans and must include photographs taken at the critical stages outlined above.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that works affecting trees are carried out in a professional and controlled manner, safeguarding their health and long-term viability. This is in accordance with good arboricultural practice.</p><div><br></div>

<p>&nbsp;All development operations, site preparation, and arboricultural works must be undertaken in strict accordance with the approved Arboricultural Impact Assessment &amp; Method Statement Report (Reference: AIA/MF/0122/26, dated June 2026) prepared by Marcus Foster, including the implementation of the Tree Protection Plan (Drawing T003).</p><p>The specified tree protection fencing and ground protection must be erected and installed prior to the commencement of any works on site and shall remain in place for the duration of the development. Notwithstanding the details provided within the approved documents, the following strict parameters apply specifically to the reconstruction of the front boundary wall within the Precautionary Areas (Root Protection Areas) of trees T4, T5, and T6:</p><p>Continuous trench excavation and traditional strip foundations are strictly prohibited.</p><p>The wall must be rebuilt using a sensitive foundation design (such as a pile and above-ground bridged lintel system) that guarantees no tree roots over 50mm in diameter are severed, pruned, or damaged during excavation or construction.</p><p>Any deviation from the approved Arboricultural Impact Assessment &amp; Method Statement (AMS) or Tree Protection Plan (TPP) requires immediate notification to the Local Planning Authority (LPA) Tree Protection Officer. In the event of such a deviation, all works within the Root Protection Areas (RPAs) of retained trees must cease immediately until an appropriate course of action has been agreed upon and approved in writing by the LPA.</p><p>REASON: To ensure the protection, retention, and long-term health of significant mature trees on and adjacent to the site, which provide crucial amenity value to the De Beauvoir Conservation Area.&nbsp;</p>
